messages:
support-oncall: :rotating_light: Customer 'Clipwise' reporting intermittent 5xx + timeouts across hosted /v1/generate endpoints since ~13:10 UTC. Multiple customers starting to hit p95 timeouts and some 504s. Escalating to war room.
ops-bot: automated alert: hosted-gateway error rate > 7% over 5m, spike at 13:12 UTC, correlated traces available at https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/178888.
alex: copying here — any known deploys around 13:05-13:15? I see a small routing canary rolled at 13:07 but no infra changes.
jamal: I can already see increased KV cache miss ratio on inference pool eu-west-1-gpu-a between 13:08-13:14, miss rate jumped from 6% -> 48%. Keys: session-prefix.*. That will amplify backend work.
maya: customer screenshot attached in support ticket: shows repeated 504 and then success. They say it affects their webhooks and causes retries.
support-oncall: repro attempt from support: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}' --max-time 10
```
Result: occasional socket timeout at ~9.8s, then 504 from gateway.
emma: working with account team to surface customer impact. Is there an obvious auth/billing correlation? logs show 200 for auth but gateway timed out waiting for inference.
raj: infra: autoscaler saw CPU on control plane spike and added a new pool at 13:13 but provisioning lag ~45s. Might explain the tail latency. I'm checking router queue lengths now.
alex: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enable fallback model routing to rw-medium-1 for the customer route only, 2) increase per-route concurrency for hosted tier temporarily, 3) purge problematic KV keys if safe. Who can apply the fallback?
jamal: I can flip fallback routing. Command: `infractl route update --route hosted/generate --fallback rw-medium-1 --constraint customer=clipwise --reason "warroom 1788888888"`
sre-lead: assign owners: jamal (runtime), raj (infra autoscale), alex (gateway routing), support-oncall/emma (customer comms). Please ack.
jamal: ack, applying fallback now.
raj: started temp-upscale of control-plane machines `asg-control-eu-west` +2, ETA ~90s.
alex: toggled per-route concurrency from 50 -> 120 for clipwise route to reduce queueing.
ops-bot: deploy event: routing update applied by jamal at 13:16:12 UTC; autoscaler delta +2 at 13:16:25 UTC.
jamal: after fallback + scale, error rate dropped: backend 5xx from 8.3% -> 1.1% within 60s, p95 latency from 2.4s -> 0.9s. P99 still slightly elevated at ~3.8s.
maya: customer on the line, they confirm fewer errors but still occasional slow requests. They're asking for ETA for full remediation and a postmortem.
alex: temporary root-cause hypothesis: combined effect of a warm routing canary that increased cold-shard fanout + sudden KV cache miss storm + control-plane scale lag. That amplified tail latencies and hit circuit breakers. Need full postmortem.
sre-lead: agreed. Immediate next steps (action items):
- jamal: collect model runtime traces and KV miss timeline (owner: jamal)
- raj: review autoscaler scaling delay and prewarm thresholds (owner: raj)
- alex: audit canary rollout config and priority queues, propose safe rollout guard (owner: alex)
- emma/maya: send interim customer update with mitigation and ETA (owner: emma)
- support-oncall: open follow-up ticket linking traces and customer report (owner: support-oncall)
Please add ETA for each.
jamal: ETA 24h for trace aggregation and initial eval, I'll attach sample flame and trace ids.
raj: ETA 48h for autoscaler postmortem and a proposal to prewarm + async attach.
alex: ETA 72h to propose rollout guard (rate-limited canary with traffic shaping).
emma: sending interim note now with mitigation summary and estimated 72h postmortem.
support-oncall: created follow-up ticket SUP-54321 linking incident traces and customer ticket.
ops-bot: note: no billing/auth correlation found in logs; token checks were green.
maya: customer asked for temporary SLA credit request path — I've routed to finance ops.
jamal: extra datapoint: KV cache eviction policy looked normal, but we saw bursty traffic from a single clipwise tenant process that created many unique session keys. Recommend request-side rate limiting or caching decorator on client.
alex: action: add a per-tenant soft-limit on concurrent long-lived sessions (short term) and an instrumentation flag to log heavy key churn. (owner: alex, ETA 7d for instrumentation).
sre-lead: please post raw timelines and candidate CL patches to the incident doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/1788888888. We'll run a blameless postmortem once owners attach artifacts.
emma: drafting the postmortem intro. Will include customer impact numbers: ~3 customers affected, ~120 failed requests in 15m window, no data loss.
support-oncall: closing war room for now — mitigations in place, monitoring for regression 30m. Reopen if error rate > 2% sustained. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: monitoring note: current hosted-gateway error rate 0.9% over 5m.
alex: quick note to infra — please keep autoscaler logs for the window; we'll need timestamps for provisioning latency.
jamal: attaching two representative trace IDs to the ticket: trace:178888-A and trace:178888-B.
raj: ack, preserving logs and enabling extended retention for the incident window.
maya: customer confirmed reduced impact and appreciates the fast response.
emma: action item summary posted to SUP-54321 and incident doc. We'll schedule a 1h postmortem meeting in 72h to go over root cause and remediation.
support-oncall: thanks team, nice coordinated run. War room closed 13:21 UTC.
